I would keep all 4.1 mu in spring peanut this year. My land is small, I have long experience, and my household only has 2 people, so I would choose a steady, manageable plan instead of anything complicated. Since I have well irrigation, I would rely on that to protect emergence and pod filling if rainfall is uneven. I would use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I would want more even emergence and better yield stability, but I would avoid anything too risky or management-heavy. For fertilization, I would keep nitrogen moderate because peanut fixes part of its own nitrogen, and I would put more emphasis on phosphorus and potassium to support rooting, flowering, and pod development. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage because it is practical on a small farm and helps prepare a fine seedbed without too much labor. I would plan a limited number of irrigations and pesticide sprays, only enough to support the crop through key stages and reduce obvious pest and disease pressure. With my experience and irrigation access, I would aim for a solid, realistic yield rather than the highest possible one.
